narrative: Markets are navigating sharp turbulence in the technology sector following the sudden resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang amid an internal probe, trade-secret espionage allegations, and potential US entity-list restrictions. This fallout has triggered a selloff across semiconductors and elevated scrutiny over non-bank debt financing rapid AI infrastructure expansion. Broader equities remain somewhat insulated, with the S&P 500 trading within range of record highs on sustained consumer strength. Oil markets are balancing Middle East geopolitical risks against rising supply from Venezuela, where Chevron is expanding output. Meanwhile, gold remains stable, functioning predominantly as household credit collateral in key physical markets, while easing inflation mitigates fears of aggressive Federal Reserve rate hikes.

Nasdaq.why: Charlie Pellet reports tech and semiconductor stocks facing heavy selling pressure down 1.34%, while Barry Ritholtz highlights the index is down 10% from highs amid China exposure and Nvidia governance risks.

S&P 500.why: Tony Crescenzi of PIMCO expects continued market growth supported by consumer resilience and data center spend, while Barry Ritholtz notes the index sits 3.3% off all-time highs and Charlie Pellet reports downside drag from tech.

Gold.why: Charlie Pellet reports gold trading virtually flat around $38.78/oz, while George Alexander Muthoot highlights its steady fundamental function as core loan collateral in India.

Oil.why: Tara Copp and Eimear Bonner highlight upward supply pressures from Middle East tensions and Chevron's Venezuelan expansion, though Bloomberg anchors report Brent and WTI trading lower into the weekend.

priced_in: Heightened volatility and valuation correction in semiconductor and mega-cap tech stocks
Strong market demand for the upcoming Anthropic IPO

debates: Equity resilience versus tech drag: Tony Crescenzi argues US consumer strength will sustain broader equity growth, while Barry Ritholtz and Charlie Pellet emphasize the drag from semiconductor corrections and China risks.

AI debt and capex sustainability: William Dudley warns of systemic financial risk from rapid debt accumulation funding AI infrastructure, contrasted with robust investor appetite evidenced by Anthropic's heavily oversubscribed IPO.
Crude balance: Upward risks from Middle East instability contrasted with expanding physical output as Chevron increases Venezuelan production from 50,000 to nearly 300,000 barrels per day.
